title: The Song for Those Who Never Returned

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: The village remembers those lost at sea: sing for them on the beach, or carve their names on the canoe house.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Every year at the start of the fishing season, the village remembers the fishers who went out and never came home. (subject)'s brother was one of them, many years ago. (friend) wants to start a new custom this year, carving the names on the canoe house, so they are not only remembered in songs. (subject) is not sure. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village gathers at sunset and sings the old song for the lost, the one that is half a lament and half a call home. (subject) sings (subject.his/her) brother's name into the waves. The tide comes in and takes the flowers. Nobody speaks for a long time afterwards.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) carves the names, one by one, onto the post of the canoe house. (subject) watches the whole time. When (subject.his/her) brother's name is done, (subject.he/she) touches it, and nods. Now the young fishers walk past the names every morning before they go out.
